references.text: Pharaoh puts Joseph in charge of all Egypt and gives him his signet ring. This is the direct context for verse 43, where Joseph is given Pharaoh's second-best chariot and 'Abrech' is cried out before him.

The psalmist praises God for making Joseph ruler over Pharaoh's house and lord over all his possessions, to bind his princes at his pleasure. This is a direct reference to Joseph's exaltation in Egypt.
Joseph explains to his brothers that it was God who sent him ahead of them and made him ruler over all Egypt. This underscores God's sovereign plan behind Joseph's rise to power.

Mordecai was clothed in royal garments and led on the king's horse through the city streets while cries were raised before him. A strong parallel to Joseph, who was led in Pharaoh's second-best chariot with the cry 'Abrech'.

Daniel was clothed in purple, given a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed as the third ruler in the kingdom. This is a parallel to Joseph's public exaltation with symbols of power and authority.
When all Egypt suffers from famine, Pharaoh sends the people to Joseph. This shows the extent of the authority Joseph received when he was elevated over the entire land of Egypt.
The New Testament verse confirms and interprets the event in Genesis as an example of God's grace and wisdom in salvation history.
